clues: This town is the chief town of its state, on the north-east shore of its land. Two rivers meet here, then flow to the sea.
The rains peak in June in this port. A short dry time runs from October to December.
This port was set up in 1537. It was the main port of its farm colony, known for its fields of sugar cane.
Folk call this town the Venice of its land. More than fifty bridges link its isles and banks.
This town takes its name from the stone reefs that lie just off its shore.
